comments.body:
INVESTIGATED BY THE OWNING SESSION, AS THIS TICKET ASKED. The observation was real and correctly
reported; the candidate root cause it offered is WRONG, and the actual cause is now fixed and proven.

Thank you for filing it rather than investigating — the "candidate, not a finding" framing was exactly
right, and the observation is what led here.

=== THE OBSERVATION IS REAL. THE STATED CAUSE IS NOT. ===

Reported: "DC inbound filing is a no-op ... no local ticket created from DC issue". The actual defect
was in the TEST'S ASSERTION, not in inbound filing. Filed and fixed as
[rebar:23ed-de0a-765b-49aa], merged as change 1124.

The assertion could never have passed, for two independent reasons:

  * `_jira_key_to_local_id` LOWERCASES (`inbound_translate.py:120-124`): `RBJNAZV-1` becomes
    `jira-rbjnazv-1`. The test's `remote_key in json.dumps(t)` check is case-sensitive.
  * the inbound CREATE payload (`apply_inbound_records.py:183-212`) carries NO raw Jira key at all —
    the key appears only as a TITLE FALLBACK, unused whenever the issue has a summary, as it does
    here ("J7 provenance oracle").

Verified against the exact payload shape the inbound path writes: `remote_key in json.dumps(ticket)`
is False. So a PERFECTLY-CREATED ticket produced a red, and a genuinely-missing one would have too —
the oracle could not distinguish them in either direction.

Also worth correcting for the record: `filed=0` in that stdout is NOT the count of tickets filed from
DC issues. `filed` counts INVARIANT-VIOLATION bug tickets (`run_differs.py:282`,
`check_at_most_one_local_id`), so `filed=0` is healthy and says nothing about inbound. `scanned=1`
and `OK: applied 1 of 1 mutations` were, in fact, consistent with a correct inbound create all along.

=== PROOF THAT INBOUND FILING WORKS ===

GitHub Actions run **30660546548**, job "jira DC harness smoke", against main @ fde6baae7 (the first
main containing the fixed oracle):

    [jira-live-canary] collected=17 executed=17 skipped=0
    1 failed, 16 passed in 13.55s

`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` **PASSED**. It now asserts:
  * a local ticket exists whose id EQUALS `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)` — exact match on the
    derived id, not a substring scan of a JSON blob;
  * the BINDING STORE maps that local id to the DC key, so the ticket corresponds to THAT issue;
  * `creation_channel == "jira"`.

`executed=17 skipped=0` matters as much as the pass count: nothing silently skipped.

The single remaining failure in that run was
`test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config`, an unrelated credential defect filed
as [rebar:cd78-d877-3d25-4ec3] and since merged.

=== WHY THIS WAS NEWLY VISIBLE, WHICH THIS TICKET GOT RIGHT ===

Your reasoning that bug 8070's fix un-masked the tier is correct, and it is worth recording that
THREE defects were masking this assertion in sequence, each hiding the next:
  1. an EMPTY store made the pass report `scanned=0` and "converged" — indistinguishable from working;
  2. the PAT-cap bug [rebar:f391-806b-938f-45d8] killed the suite at SETUP before the test ran;
  3. the oracle itself could not pass (23ed).
Only with all three fixed does this test's verdict carry information.

DISPOSITION: closing as a duplicate of [rebar:23ed-de0a-765b-49aa], which is the same underlying issue
diagnosed to its actual cause and already fixed, merged and closed. No inbound-filing defect exists.

## REOPENED — this ticket closed WITHOUT a completion-verifier attestation

Operator ruling: a close without completion verification is prohibited. This ticket is `closed` with an empty `attestations` map — no `completion-verifier` record — so it never passed the gate.

**It is one of exactly two such tickets in epic e369's 41-descendant tree**, and together they are why the epic could not be certified. `gate_ops.py:129` sets `certifiable = not uncertified`, documented at the line:

> Certification is WITHHELD iff a direct child is closed-but-UNCERTIFIED (force-closed): the parent MAY close but cannot be certified — certification propagates, so an unattested descendant withholds the parent's signature.

So e369 closed with a PASS verdict and no signature, purely because this ticket and [rebar:2bc7-d77b-641c-42aa]/[rebar:0059-c7f0-cce1-4077] were unattested. Reopening is the documented remedy: move it back to `in_progress` and re-close through the gate, which mints the attestation and unblocks the epic's certification.

**Re-close it on its own merits, not to unblock the epic.** If its acceptance criteria are genuinely met the gate will say so; if they are not, that is a real finding and this ticket should stay open. Note the completion verifier has been repaired since these closes — [rebar:1019-e1e9-5117-4795] — so a re-close now runs a gate that can actually see.

## RE-CLOSE-0059-A: re-closed on its own merits through a gate that can now see

Reopened because the original close carried no completion-verifier attestation. Re-verified both
acceptance criteria independently before re-closing; neither rests on the epic's need to certify.

**AC1 — mechanism identified and cited, and the 5f48-duplicate question settled.** The reported
symptom (`scanned=1 filed=0`, "no local ticket created from DC issue") was real; its stated cause was
not. The defect was in the test's own oracle, not in inbound filing:

  * `_jira_key_to_local_id` lowercases (`inbound_translate.py:120-124`), so `RBJNAZV-1` becomes
    `jira-rbjnazv-1` and the cell's case-sensitive `remote_key in json.dumps(t)` scan could not match;
  * the inbound CREATE payload (`apply_inbound_records.py:183-212`) carries no raw Jira key at all —
    the key appears only as a title fallback, unused whenever the issue has a summary.

So the oracle could not distinguish a perfectly-created ticket from a missing one in EITHER direction.
Separately, `filed` counts invariant-violation bug tickets (`run_differs.py:282`,
`check_at_most_one_local_id`), so `filed=0` was healthy and said nothing about inbound at all.

Not a duplicate of 5f48 (the silent identity-mint failure) — that was the filing ticket's own candidate
hypothesis and it is wrong. It IS the same underlying issue as [rebar:23ed-de0a-765b-49aa], which
diagnosed it to this cause and fixed it (merged as change 1124). Closing as a duplicate of 23ed.

**AC2 — the cell passes against the live DC harness.** `executed=17 skipped=0`, with
`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` passing on an assertion that now has
reach: exact equality against `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)`, the binding store mapping that local
id to the DC key, and `creation_channel == "jira"`. The `skipped=0` matters as much as the pass count.

No inbound-filing defect exists. Three defects had masked this assertion in sequence — an empty store
reporting `scanned=0`, the PAT-cap bug [rebar:f391-806b-938f-45d8] killing setup, then the oracle itself
— which is why the verdict only became informative once all three were fixed.

## Reported by, not investigated by, an adjacent session

Surfaced while confirming the fix for bug 8070 (external-integration canary). Per operator
instruction this was NOT investigated — epic e369 is actively held by another session and owns this
subject matter. Filing it here so the owning session sees it. **The root cause below is a candidate,
not a finding.**

## Observed (live CI, reproducible)

Run 30651750699 — `workflow_dispatch` of `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` on `main` at
commit `b7e6ac963`, 2026-07-31. Job **"jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)"**:

```
tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py:319
AssertionError: no local ticket was created from DC issue RBJNAZV-1;
  stdout='invariants: scanned=1 filed=0 (cap=5)\nOK: applied 1 of 1 mutations\n'
assert []
FAILED test_reconcile_pass.py::test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance
```

The failing test is `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance`.

## Why this is newly visible

This failure was previously MASKED. Until `b7e6ac963` the whole external tier died at
`SnapshotRefError` on an unborn `HEAD` before reaching any behaviour under test (bug 8070). With
snapshot resolution fixed, the tier now reaches its subject and this assertion fails on its merits.
So this is very likely a pre-existing defect that the canary could not previously report, not a new
regression from `b7e6ac963` — which touched only `tests/external/conftest.py` (adds an empty root
commit) and added a unit test.

## Candidate cause — UNCONFIRMED, do not treat as diagnosed

`scanned=1 filed=0` says the inbound record was seen and then not filed. That shape is consistent
with OPEN bug **5f48-244c-7063-42d0** — "DC inbound identity mint fails silently: 'jira-datacenter'
is not a valid creation_channel" — where a silent mint failure would drop the record between scan
and file. Linked `relates_to`. If that is the cause, this ticket is a duplicate and should be closed
as such rather than worked separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The mechanism behind `scanned=1 filed=0` is identified and cited (`path:line`), and it is
      determined whether this is the same defect as 5f48 (close as duplicate) or distinct.
- [ ] `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` passes against the live DC
      harness, or the failure is guarded by a credential-free test in the default suite.
